Evelyn / Michael —

Draft below is what I plan to send to Greenleaf. Please review for accuracy and legal tone. I kept answers concise and mapped them to the questionnaire items.

1) Data residency (hosted API)
- Answer: Redwood hosts customer workloads in region-specific clusters. For hosted API customers, we can restrict data storage and processing to a single region (US or EU) depending on the account configuration and billing region. Region restriction applies to request payloads, model inference state (KV/prefix caches), and customer logs.
- Notes: Region restriction is enforced at the storage and routing level; metadata used for telemetry (anonymized metrics) is aggregated and not customer-identifiable.

2) Default retention windows
- Request/response logs and traces (hosted API): default 30 days; configurable to 0/7/30/90/365 days per account on request.
- Diagnostic debug artifacts (rare, by support request): stored for a maximum of 90 days unless customer requests earlier deletion.
- KV/prefix cache (inference runtime): ephemeral by design; per-session TTLs typically mirror the API session (default 1 hour) and are not persisted to long-term storage by default. Cached keys are evicted according to an LRU policy; they are not included in long-term backups.

3) Deletion and DSR workflow
- Answer: Customers may request data deletion via the Console (Account > Data Settings) or via a deletion API/Support ticket. Once a deletion request is received, Redwood purges active storage and related logs within the contracted SLA window (typically 72 hours for hosted API customers).
- Backups/formal restore points are also indexed; we schedule a complementary purge in backup catalogs to complete within 30 days of the initial deletion operation. We provide a deletion certificate for contractual records upon completion.

4) Backups and disaster recovery
- Answer: Regular backups exist to meet durability SLAs. For hosted API accounts scoped to a single region we keep backups in that region by default; cross-region replication only occurs if configured by customer (or for Dedicated/private deployments where DR policy requires it). Backups are retained for 30 days by default and are included in the backup purge schedule tied to deletion requests.

5) Use for model training
- Answer: By default, customer content is not used to improve or train Redwood models. Any training/analytics using customer data requires a documented opt-in and contractual terms.

6) Auditability and evidence
- Answer: We can provide audit logs (who requested deletion, timestamps, job ids), and a deletion certificate. We maintain SOC2-type operational logs for platform actions; redacted examples can be shared under NDA.

7) Exceptions and contractual controls
- Answer: Specific retention windows, region guarantees, and deletion SLAs can be contractually committed for enterprise accounts (Dedicated or Private deployments) and for hosted API under an addendum.

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for sending the questionnaire. Please find our formal responses attached (PDF) and a short FAQ below that maps each answer to your numbered items. If Greenleaf wants a contractual SLA for 100% US-only storage and a 7-day retention for logs, we can produce an addendum for review (note: very short retention windows may impact our ability to diagnose incidents).

Key points (summary):
- Region guarantee: Hosted API accounts can be scoped to US-only processing/storage. We enforce this at the routing and storage layers.
- Default retention (hosted API): 30 days for request/response logs and traces; options available down to 0/7/30/90/365 days via account settings or addendum.
- Deletion: Deletion requests are processed within 72 hours for active storage; backup purges completed within 30 days and a deletion certificate is provided.
- KV/prefix caching: Runtime caches are ephemeral (default 1-hour TTL), not persisted to long-term backups, and evicted by LRU.
- Training: Customer content is not used for model training without explicit opt-in and a signed agreement.
